title: Positive fibre degrees give a projective-bundle embedding
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes (each has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), and suppose each geometric fibre has dimension at most $1$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every geometric point $x\to X$ and each one-dimensional irreducible component $Z$ of the reduced fibre $Y_x$, the degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] of $\mathcal L$ pulled back to the normalization of $Z$ is positive. Then $\mathcal L$ is $f$-ample: over each affine open $U\subset X$ its restriction is an ample invertible module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There is a positive integer $n$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ with a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_X(\mathcal E)$ pulling back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$. Thus $f$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre], and dimension is [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Normalization of an integral component has the meaning of [def-sc-normalization].

source.place: Stacks Tags 0B5Y, varieties.tex, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components (normalization degree is unchanged by finite birational pullback); 0D2S, more-morphisms.tex, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood; 01VU, morphisms.tex, lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample and lemma-relatively-very-ample. Proper coherent pushforward makes f_*L^n finite type; properness makes its immersion closed.
